back: Current assets ÷ current liabilities, written x : 1.
(Current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities, written x : 1.
The ability of a business to pay its short-term debts as they fall due.
Current assets − current liabilities (net current assets).

front: Why exclude inventory from the acid test?
back: Inventory must be sold and then paid for before it becomes cash, so it is the least liquid current asset.
May mean too much inventory, slow debt collection or idle cash that could earn a return.
Collect debts faster, reduce inventory, introduce capital, take a long-term loan instead of an overdraft, cut drawings, get longer supplier credit.
ZIMSEC: quick ratio. Cambridge: acid test (liquid) ratio. Same formula.
